From the game director, for Tom: the half-hour duels, cause and proposal. Nothing is built yet.

Cause:
1. Tiredness slows a man's blow and guard but never his eyes or hand control. After 3–4 minutes the defender has about 3× the spare time to parry, so nearly every blow is parried. Tiredness also stops growing there, and rests give back breath only.
2. Two men both at breaking point each wait for an opening and never strike. Nothing pushes either over the edge, so they stand until the bell. A code comment says a spent man keeps wearing down; the code doesn't do it.

Real life: fine control fails first when exhausted, reading the opponent worsens, men clinch, rests don't restore, and spent men end fights through mistakes.

Every option includes a "standoff fix": a man stuck at his breaking point wears down until he steadies or gives up.
- A, tired eyes: tiredness slows his sight too. Half-hour skilled duels go from 91 to 9 in 5000. Changes the fight from minute one, and Attack counts less.
- B, tired hands (pick): once properly tired, a parry sometimes fails, up to 1 in 5 when fully spent. Half-hour duels go to 0. Fresh fighting untouc
